P1.evidence: No setter — the prospect came directly from an Instagram advert. Same compressed three-part frame the rep uses throughout, missing what is in the way and what you need. A light agreement was sought on time rather than on the frame: 'We have a limited amount of time, so shall we dive into it?' — 'Yeah, go ahead.' Open question ran verbatim: 'How can we potentially help you, my friend?'

P2.evidence: Mechanically the most complete baseline in the batch and substantively the most dangerous. Five checks ran properly and in sequence: weight (118 kg), height (5'11"), age (52), then 'Monday to Sunday, what does your exercise regimen look like at the moment?' and 'how long have you been following this kind of routine for?', then energy on a one-to-ten scale, then 'would you say you're waking up rested or not?', then 'finally, your diet, is that dialed in?' followed by 'how's your food?'. That is textbook. And then the two checks that carry all the risk were skipped entirely. Health conditions were never asked — sleep apnea was volunteered inside the energy answer ('I had sleep apnea too, so now I got a device that's helping me') and drew no follow-up. Injuries were never asked, and at 01:12:14 the prospect volunteered a worsening back injury that had ended his swimming: 'my back is getting worse... then my back's got bad, really bad. I hurt my back.' Not one question followed. A 52-year-old at roughly BMI 36 with a deteriorating back and untreated-until-recently sleep apnea completed a full baseline in which neither condition was enquired about.

P3.evidence: The deep-goal work did not happen. The bridge was attempted properly — 'would you say that you are 100% happy with your health and wellness at the moment?' got a fast no, and 'why not' and 'what are you noticing on a day-to-day basis' both ran — but the prospect closed the door hard: 'nothing bad. I just see the fact that I'm overweight and that I'm getting old, but I'm happy and present, so it doesn't hurt me at all.' The rep accepted that and never found another route in. P3f and P3g never ran at all, which is the notable failure: he has a wife and sons who are all fit, sons who train in a home gym he does not use, and he had already framed the decision in legacy terms ('if I want to live long'). Ripple, family and identity were all available and none were touched. P3c is a specific miss too — he can no longer swim because of his back, which is the clearest 'something physical you want to do but can't' in the batch, and it went by unremarked.

P4.evidence: P4c ran directly and well — 'Why haven't you got this routine in the past 10 years then?' — and P4f ran in its intended form: 'what is the rationale in terms of having outside help as opposed to doing it yourself?'. But P4e was undermined by the rep supplying the answer instead of eliciting it: 'would you say that part of the reason that you haven't been able to get into your ideal body for the past 10 years is due to a bit of comfort, being a bit comfortable?' is a leading question, and the prospect simply agreed. When the rep then asked why, the answer that came back was different and more useful than the one supplied — 'it's not a priority for me. For me, priority has been business, kids' — which is a prioritisation problem, not a comfort problem, and the phase never adjusted.

P5.evidence: Nothing ran. No two-year question, no settle-for, no why-not, no line in the sand. This is the fifth consecutive call in the batch with no consequence frame, and on this call it is the most consequential omission of all: a 52-year-old at roughly BMI 36 with sleep apnea and a deteriorating back, who explicitly said his current position does not bother him ('I'm happy and present, so it doesn't hurt me at all'), is the exact prospect the phase exists for. The cost of inaction was the entire case and it was never made.

P6.evidence: The alignment check ran before the price, which is correct, and returned an explicitly conditional non-answer: 'the first question in my mind is, can I do this with just by watching YouTube... I'll give it a try and see how it goes, if the price is within the range of what I can pay.' That is not a yes; it is a stated precondition. The rep replied 'Okay, give it a try and see where it takes you' and moved directly to the four price levels. The belief question and the all-in question were never asked. Because there was no clear yes and no consequence frame behind it, the price landed on nothing and the call ended forty seconds later.

P11.evidence: The prospect declined at the price and no part of payment or onboarding became reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger could not have been clearer — 'that's out of my range... it's just too much for me... it's not within our budget' — and exactly one move ran. The isolation was correct and correctly placed: 'Putting the investment aside for a second, do you feel like you actually want to do this?', answered 'Yeah, I mean, I do want to do this.' At that point the play calls for the how-not-whether reframe, the payment-plan invitation and the financial picture. None of it ran. The rep asked 'what is going to be the plan for yourself from this point on?', heard that the prospect would go and find an app, and wished him well. Worth setting against the Brandon Johnson call the previous day, where the same rep ran the complete financial interrogation on a prospect in active bankruptcy proceedings. Here a business owner who said the price was out of range was asked nothing and released inside a minute. The play is being applied with wide and unexplained variance.

Doubt was live in two distinct forms and neither was addressed. First, efficacy doubt from direct experience: 'we did use a membership for my son, where one of them was actually online, like this was not helpful at all.' The BURNED BEFORE move exists in the playbook for precisely this and did not run. Second, and more importantly, he named his own decision criterion out loud — 'making sure that the movements are right, I'm not injuring myself. That's the key' — which is simultaneously the doubt to resolve and the programme's central feature. The weekly form-review loop had been described eight minutes earlier and was never connected to it.
No request for time; he declined outright.
His wife featured in the diet discussion and in 'it's not within our budget', but never as an approval gate.
He had already decided the timing was now — 'this year, this will be my priority number one'.

Free-substitute objection in its most complete form, raised by the prospect as his opening question at the alignment check and never answered: YouTube for the movements, a fully equipped home gym downstairs, sons who train and could show him, and a self-built walking programme that is already producing results he is pleased with. The known script gap assumes a cheap paid alternative; here every substitute is free and one of them is currently working. Nothing in the playbook addresses it.

Price opacity as a stated grievance, and worth escalating as a process finding rather than a rep failure: 'I wish you guys, I think on your website, you should actually write those prices.' A prospect anchored at $100-200 per month spent twenty-five minutes on a closing call before learning the entry price is $1,200 and the programme is $4,000 to $9,000. There is no qualification step, in the script or apparently in the setting process, that would have caught this.

notes: A short call that shows both halves of this rep clearly. The mechanical baseline was the best in the batch — age, height, weight, training week, diet, sleep and energy all asked in sequence — and the two checks that carried real risk, health conditions and injuries, were skipped, on a prospect who volunteered sleep apnea and a worsening back injury unprompted. After that, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and a price presented to a stated conditional. The coaching point is narrow and specific: when a prospect volunteers a spinal injury, stop and ask about it. The business points are that the $1,200 product was presented here as a standard tier having been presented as an off-menu exception twice in the previous twenty-four hours, and that nothing upstream of this call filtered a prospect anchored at $100 a month.
